subject: Clarify derivative claims & feedback license language for Order Form
messages:
From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@brightco.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightCo Legal <legal@brightco.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — ownership & training questions

Jonas —

Thanks for the walkthrough today. Our legal team attached a marked-up Order Form focused on the IP and product-use sections. Two quick asks they flagged:

1) They want explicit confirmation that BrightCo retains exclusive ownership of any customer-provided content, and that Redwood will not claim ownership of BrightCo output in ways that interfere with downstream productization.
2) They asked for a carveout to prevent BrightCo-generated content from being used to train Redwood-wide models (we proposed a feedback license but they want more control).

Attached: BrightCo_OrderForm_redlines.docx (redlines), and a short note from legal. Can your team propose a clean, negotiable clause we can include in the Order Form (or an appendix) that addresses both points while keeping the language reasonably standard for SaaS + inference providers?

We're targeting sign-off by the end of next week — appreciate any compromise language you can send that the legal team can review.

Best,
Megan Liu
Head of Partnerships, BrightCo
megan.liu@brightco.com
(415) 555-0199

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@brightco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 12:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — ownership & training questions

Megan —

Thanks for sending the redlines and for the clear summary. We're sympathetic to BrightCo's need to protect customer content. High level proposal from our side:

- Customer Content: BrightCo retains all ownership in Customer Content (as you requested). Redwood will only store and process Customer Content to provide the Service and will not assert ownership over that content.

- Output / Derivative Rights: We can confirm BrightCo gets a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Output for their productization efforts subject to any export/control rules and the usual restrictions on harassment/illegal uses. We want to preserve Redwood's ability to show anonymized, aggregated examples for ops/monitoring and to improve service quality.

- Training / Feedback License: We are prepared to include a narrow opt-out for training on BrightCo Customer Content and BrightCo-specific Output. Proposal: an explicit checkbox in the Order Form that states BrightCo opts out of Redwood using Customer Content and BrightCo Output to train general Redwood models. If unchecked, Redwood gets a limited, non-exclusive feedback license for the purposes of debugging, improving the service, and safety monitoring, with use restrictions (no model weights transfer or sublicensing).

I'm looping in Laura from Legal and Ben from Sales to craft the precise redline we can offer back. Laura — can you draft two short redline options: (A) customer opt-out by default (no training unless customer opts in) and (B) the checkbox approach (opt-in/opt-out toggle) with clear language covering aggregated/anonymized usage and limitations? We'd like to keep the Order Form simple so procurement doesn't get blocked.

Thanks — we'll attach a text snippet for you to send to BrightCo legal.

Jonas Weber
VP Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Liu <megan.liu@brightco.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — ownership & training questions

Jonas / Ben —

Drafting two compact options below for the Order Form (keeps the MSA intact, inserts into Order Form section titled "Use of Customer Content and Feedback"). Please review and tell me which to send to BrightCo. I also attached a plain-text file with the same snippets (proposed_feedback_license_snippet.txt) for easy ingestion into DocuSign.

Option A — Default Opt-Out (strongest customer protection)
"Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Content and any Output generated by the Service that specifically incorporates or is derived from Customer Content. Redwood shall not use Customer Content or such Output to train, improve or develop Redwood’s foundational or general-purpose models, or otherwise incorporate Customer Content or such Output into any model weights, without Customer’s prior written consent. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry for the sole purpose of maintaining and operating the Service, subject to the restrictions in Section X (Data Handling)."

Option B — Checkbox Opt-Out (configurable in Order Form)
"Customer may elect, by checking the box in the Order Form, to opt-out of Redwood using Customer Content and Output for the training or improvement of Redwood’s general-purpose models. If Customer does not check the opt-out box, Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use Customer Content and Output solely to improve and develop the Service, subject to (i) removal of Customer-identifying metadata, (ii) prohibition on sublicensing standalone model weights that incorporate Customer Content, and (iii) use restricted to safety, reliability and performance improvements. Redwood will not assert ownership in Customer Content or Customer Output."

Notes / tradeoffs: Option A reduces product-side upside (we can't learn patterns across customers) and increases cost for BrightCo (no shared improvements). Option B is a practical compromise and is closer to market norm; it gives BrightCo control and keeps an operational pathway for Redwood improvements.

If you want, I can also draft a short addendum that limits the license to a 12-month training window after which Customer Content must be deleted from training datasets — that can be appealing to some enterprise buyers.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — ownership & training questions

Thanks Jonas / Laura —

BrightCo legal reviewed the two options. They prefer Option B (checkbox opt-out) with one small tweak: the opt-out should explicitly prevent use of BrightCo Output to train models that are sold or licensed outside the Redwood service (i.e., no transfer of BrightCo-influenced weights to third-party model products). Your Option B already prohibits sublicensing of standalone model weights, but they asked that we add the explicit phrase below (inserted in italics in the clause):

"... and (iii) use restricted to safety, reliability and performance improvements, and shall not be used to train or produce models or model weights that are licensed, sold, or otherwise provided to third parties outside the Service."

If you can confirm that language is acceptable, we can update the redline and move to signatures. Happy to take the checkbox approach — thanks for keeping this concise.

Best,
Megan Liu
Head of Partnerships, BrightCo
